source_text: PAX ecce, dilectissimi fratres, Ecclesiae reddita est et, quod difficile nuper incredulis ac perfidis impossibile videbatur, ope atque ultione divina securitas nostra reparata est. In laetitiam mentes redeunt, et, tempestate pressurae ac nube discussa, tranquillitas ac serenitas refulserunt. Dandae laudes Deo, et beneficia ejus ac munera cum gratiarum actione celebranda, quamvis agere gratias nostra vox nec in persecutione cessaverit. Neque enim tantum inimico licere potest ut non, qui Dominum toto corde et anima et virtute diligimus, benedictiones ejus et laudes semper et ubique cum gloria praedicemus. Exoptatus votis omnium dies venit, et, post longae noctis horribilem tetramque caliginem, Domini luce radiatus mundus eluxit. Confessores, praeconio boni nominis claros et virtutis ac fidei laudibus gloriosos, laetis conspectibus intuemur, sanctis osculis adhaerentes, desideratos diu inexplebili cupiditate complectimur. Adest militum Christi cohors candida, qui persecutionis urgentus ferociam turbulentam stabili congressione fregerunt, parati ad patientiam carceris, armati ad tolerantiam mortis. Repugnastis fortiter saeculo, spectaculum gloriosum praebuistis Deo, secuturis fratribus fuistis exemplo. Religiosa vox Christum locuta est, in quem se semel credidisse confessa est. Illustres manus, quae non nisi divinis operibus assueverant, sacrificiis sacrilegis restiterunt. Sanctificata ora coelestibus cibis, post corpus et sanguinem Domini, profana contagia et idolorum reliquias respuerunt. Ab impio sceleratoque velamine, quo illic velabantur sacrificantium capita captiva, caput vestrum liberum mansit. Frons cum signo Dei pura, diaboli coronam ferre non potuit, coronae se Domini reservavit. Quam vos laete sinu suo excipit mater Ecclesia de praelio revertentes! quam beata, quam gaudens portas suas aperit, ut adunatis agminibus intretis, de hoste prostrato trophaea referentes! Cum triumphantibus viris et feminae veniunt, quae cum saeculo dimicantes, sexum quoque vicerunt. Veniunt et geminata militiae suae gloria virgines, et pueri annos suos virtutibus transeuntes. Necnon et caetera stantium multitudo vestram gloriam sequitur, proximis et pene conjunctis laudis insignibus vestigia vestra comitatur. Eadem et in illis sinceritas cordis, eadem fidei tenacis integritas. Inconcussis praeceptorum coelestium radicibus nixos et evangelicis traditionibus roboratos, non praescripta exilia, non destinata tormenta, non rei familiaris damna, non corporis supplicia terruerunt. Explorandae fidei praefiniebantur dies. Sed qui saeculo renuntiasse se meminit, nullum saeculi diem novit; nec tempora terrena jam computat qui aeternitatem de Deo sperat. Nemo, fratres dilectissimi, nemo hanc gloriam mutilet, nemo incorruptam stantium firmitatem maligna obtrectatione debilitet. Cum dies negantibus praestitutus excessit, quisquis professus intra diem non est, Christianum se esse confessus est. Primus est victoriae titulus, gentilium manibus apprehensum Dominum confiteri: secundus ad gloriam gradus est cauta secessione subtractum Domino reservari. Illa publica, haec privata confessio est. Ille judicem saeculi vincit, hic contentus Deo suo judice conscientiam puram cordis integritate custodit. Illic, fortitudo promptior, hic sollicitudo securior. Ille appropinquante hora sua, jam maturus inventus est; hic fortasse dilatus est qui, patrimonio derelicto, idcirco secessit quia non erat negaturus: confiteretur utique si fuisset et ipse detentus. Has martyrum coelestes coronas, has confessorum glorias spiritales, has stantium fratrum maximas eximiasque virtutes moestitia una contristat, quod avulsam nostrorum viscerum partem violentus inimicus populationis suae strage dejecit. Quid hoc loco faciam, dilectissimi fratres? fluctuans vario mentis aestu, quid aut quomodo dicam? Lacrymis magis quam verbis opus est ad exprimendum dolorem quo corporis nostri plaga deflenda est, quo populi aliquando numerosi multiplex lamentanda jactura est. Quis enim sic durus aut ferreus, quis sic fraternae charitatis oblitus, qui inter suorum multiformes ruinas et lugubres ac multo squalore deformes reliquias constitutus siccos oculos tenere praevaleat, nec, erumpente statim fletu, prius gemitus suos lacrymis quam voce depromat? Doleo, fratres, doleo vobiscum, nec mihi ad leniendos dolores meos integritas propria et sanitas privata blanditur, quando plus pastor in gregis sui vulnere vulneretur. Cum singulis pectus meum copulo, moeroris et funeris pondera luctuosa participo. Cum plangentibus plango, cum deflentibus defleo, cum jacentibus jacere me credo. Jaculis illis grassantis inimici mea simul membra percussa sunt, saevientes gladii per mea viscera transierunt. Immunis et liber a persecutionis incursu fuisse non potest animus. In prostratis fratribus et me prostravit affectus.
pass_a_gloss: Behold, most beloved brothers, peace has been restored to the Church, and what recently seemed impossible to unbelievers and the faithless, our security has been restored by divine aid and vengeance. Minds are returning to joy, and with the storm of oppression and the cloud dispersed, tranquility and serenity have shone forth. Praises must be given to God, and His benefits and gifts must be celebrated with thanksgiving, although our voice did not cease to give thanks even in persecution. For it is not possible for the enemy to be allowed so much that those who love the Lord with their whole heart and soul and strength do not always and everywhere proclaim His blessings and praises with glory. The day longed for by all has arrived, and after the horrible and dark night, the world has shone forth radiant with the Lord's light. We gaze upon the confessors, renowned for their good name and glorious for their virtues and faith, with joyful countenances, clinging to them with holy kisses, embracing them with unquenchable longing. The white cohort of Christ's soldiers is present, who broke the fierce and turbulent fury of persecution with a stable confrontation, prepared for the patience of prison, armed for the tolerance of death. You have resisted the world strongly, you have presented a glorious spectacle to God, you have been an example to your brothers who will follow. The religious voice has spoken Christ, in whom it has confessed to have believed once. Illustrious hands, which were accustomed only to divine works, have resisted sacrilegious sacrifices. Mouths sanctified by heavenly food, after the body and blood of the Lord, have rejected profane contagions and the remnants of idols. Your head has remained free from the impious and wicked veil with which the heads of those sacrificing were captive. Your forehead, with the sign of God, pure, could not bear the devil's crown, it has reserved itself for the Lord's crown. How gladly the mother Church receives you, returning from battle, with open arms! How blessed, how joyful she opens her gates, that you may enter with gathered troops, bringing back trophies from the prostrate enemy! With the triumphant men, women also come, who, fighting with the world, have also conquered their sex. The virgins also come, with double glory of their military service, and boys, who have surpassed their years with virtues. And the rest of the multitude of the standing also follows your glory, with proximate and almost conjoint insignia of praise, they accompany your footsteps. The same sincerity of heart, the same tenacity of faith, is in them. Rooted in the unshaken roots of heavenly precepts and strengthened by evangelical traditions, they were not terrified by prescribed exiles, nor destined torments, nor losses of family, nor bodily punishments. Days were set apart for testing faith. But he who remembers that he has renounced the world knows no day of the world; nor does he who hopes for eternity from God now compute earthly times. No one, most beloved brothers, no one must mutilate this glory, no one must weaken the incorrupt firmness of the standing with malignant detraction. When the day set for those who deny has passed, whoever has not professed within the day has confessed that he is a Christian. The first title of victory is to confess the Lord, apprehended by the hands of the Gentiles; the second step to glory is to be reserved for the Lord by cautious secession. The former is public, the latter private confession. The former conquers the judge of the world, the latter, content with his own judge, God, keeps a pure conscience with the integrity of heart. There, fortitude is more prompt; here, solicitude is more secure. There, he who is approaching his hour has already been found mature; here, perhaps, he who has been delayed, having abandoned his patrimony, has done so because he was not going to deny: he would have confessed, certainly, if he had also been detained. These heavenly crowns of martyrs, these spiritual glories of confessors, these greatest and most excellent virtues of standing brothers, one sorrow afflicts, that the violent enemy has thrown down a torn part of our bowels with the destruction of his population. What shall I do in this place, most beloved brothers? Fluctuating with various waves of mind, what or how shall I say? Tears are needed more than words to express the grief with which the wound of our body must be lamented, with which the multiple loss of our once numerous people must be mourned. For who is so hard or iron-like, who is so forgetful of fraternal charity, that, established among the many and mournful ruins and the squalid and deformed remnants of his own, he can prevail in keeping his eyes dry, and not, with tears bursting forth immediately, pour out his groans in tears rather than in voice? I grieve, brothers, I grieve with you, nor does my own integrity and private health flatter me in alleviating my grief, when the shepherd is wounded more in the wound of his flock. My heart is joined with each one, I participate in the mournful weights of sorrow and funeral. I lament with those who lament, I mourn with those who mourn, I believe I am lying down with those who are lying down. The darts of the raging enemy have struck my members at the same time, the raging swords have passed through my bowels. The mind cannot have been immune and free from the attack of persecution. In the prostrate brothers, affection has also prostrated me.
